goal: Compare the methods reported in the three uploaded papers with experiment.xlsx results. Find the best configuration under 3M parameters, generate a chart, and assess whether our results support the reported design advantages. Use only uploaded data and documents; these are synthetic fixtures.
answer:
## Comparison

| Method | Reported method | Parameters | mIoU | Eligible under strict <3M? |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | Convolutional segmentation | 2.5M | 73.27 | Yes [paper_1.pdf, p.1] |
| B | Attention segmentation | 3.2M | 76.0 | No [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7] |
| C | Compact convolution baseline | 2.0M | 70.0 | Yes [paper_3.pdf, p.1] |

All three sources label these as synthetic test values, use the same fixture benchmark/evaluation protocol, and claim descriptive quality/cost tradeoffs only, with no causal or ablation claim [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1].

The uploaded `experiment.xlsx` contains exactly A 2.5M/73.27, B 3.2M/76.0, C 2.0M/70.0 [Analysis 7563f4aa-7f9c-4660-ac5c-45b7b34be6ec]. Its dataset ID maps to `experiment.xlsx` in the analysis context [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7]. The worksheet values match the reported synthetic fixture values.

## Best configuration under 3M

The computed `rank_under_budget` operation with constraint `params_m < 3.0` gives eligible models A (2.5M, 73.27) and C (2.0M, 70.0); `best` is **A** [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7]. B is 3.2M, outside the strict <3M budget, and should not be selected even though it appears first in the raw ranked list [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7].

## Do results support reported design advantages?

The reported numeric deltas are A over C: +3.27 mIoU at +0.5M parameters; B over A: +2.73 mIoU at +0.7M parameters [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. The worksheet reproduces the same values [Analysis 7563f4aa-7f9c-4660-ac5c-45b7b34be6ec], so it is descriptively consistent with those reports.

It does **not** validate the methods’ design advantages as causal or architectural claims. The sources explicitly limit themselves to descriptive tradeoffs and make no causal/ablation claims [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. They also report no uncertainty estimates [paper_3.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_1.pdf, p.1].

## Artifacts, gaps, and contradictions

The computed output reports chart `comparison.png` [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7]; the provided evidence does not include visual inspection or validation of its contents.

Unresolved observed inconsistency: the `rank_under_budget` raw `ranked` list places B (3.2M) first despite the `<3.0` constraint; the `eligible`/`best` fields exclude B and select A [Analysis 06ae21ec-16f4-4deb-b43e-359e089bf5e7]. Use the eligible/best output for budget-constrained selection, but the raw list is internally inconsistent as shown. Statistical meaningfulness remains unresolved given no uncertainty estimates [paper_3.pdf, p.1].
